extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers interested in U.S. congressional hearings, wartime inquiries, and pending legislation
extracted.subtask_description: Contemporary news reporting of Congressional hearings, government investigations, and related legislative proposals (e.g., hearings on foreign policy, Pearl Harbor inquiries, and a proposed labor fact‑finding bill). Summarizes testimony, committee procedure, and bill text excerpts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of Disputes (Secretary of Labor findings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sec. 2. Whenever the Secretary of Labor finds—(1) That there is a labor dispute in which the agencies of the government charged with the functions of mediation and conciliation have been unable to [resolve it]; and (2) That a stoppage of work seriously affecting the national public interest and affecting interstate or foreign commerce, or the national defense, or commerce within the District of Columbia or any territory or possession of the United States, has resulted or threatens to result from such dispute, the Secretary shall certify such findings to the President.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any such certification of the Secretary shall be published in 'The Federal Register' and shall designate the employer or employers involved in such dispute, the groups or units of employees involved in such dispute, and the representative or representatives of such employees. (When representation is in dispute, the Secretary may request the NLRB to certify names under the National Labor Relations Act.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential appointment of fact-finding boards
rubrics_metrics.description: Sec. 3. (A) At any time within five days after the date of such certification by the Secretary of Labor, the President, in his discretion, may appoint a board to investigate such labor dispute and to make a report containing its findings of fact and recommendations with respect to such dispute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The board shall be composed of three or more persons, none of whom has any pecuniary or other private interest in the employers or employees who are parties to the dispute. The board shall proceed expeditiously to make a thorough investigation of all facts it deems relevant, give the parties a full and fair hearing (in person or by counsel/representatives), allow presentation of evidence, and within twenty days after appointment submit its report to the President. The time for submitting the report may be extended by agreement of the parties with Presidential approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality and procedural protections for fact-finding boards
rubrics_metrics.description: Boards must include persons 'none of whom has any pecuniary or other private interest' in the dispute and must give parties a 'full and fair hearing' with opportunity to present evidence and be represented by counsel or representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boards are to proceed expeditiously, conduct thorough investigations of relevant facts, allow parties to present evidence in support of their claims, and submit findings and recommendations within statutory timeframes (20 days, with possible extension by agreement plus Presidential approval).

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of the National Labor Relations Board in representation disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: When a question arises concerning the representation of such employees, the Secretary of Labor may request the National Labor Relations Board to certify to him the names of the representatives of such employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NLRB shall determine the names of such representatives in the manner provided in Section 9 of the National Labor Relations Act; this is the prescribed procedure for resolving representation questions prior to or during fact-finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: UNRRA appropriations and 'free press' restriction (Brown amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Brown's amendment would prohibit use of UNRRA appropriation funds in countries which deny American reporters free access to news of UNRRA activities there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senate removed the rider from the $550,000,000 appropriation by voice vote; the sponsor indicated an intent to try attaching the amendment to another UNRRA measure. Debate centers on legislative vehicle appropriateness (Senator McKellar argued the appropriation bill was no place for such restrictions) and on ensuring public accountability for aid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling classified/foreign-origin documents in committee hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: When a witness offers to submit documents of 'great importance to the foreign policy of the United States' that were originally sent from China in code, the committee should receive them only in secret session and take them up with the State Department privately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because originals may be coded, the committee may paraphrase or place public summaries in the record rather than publish originals; witnesses may be asked to submit lists of documents for in-camera review; witnesses may be cautioned about partisanship and allowed to decline public release of sensitive materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diplomatic emergency 'winds' code protocol (prearranged signal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of certain words in a Tokyo/noon radio broadcast (e.g., the reported code words like 'east rain' or 'west wind clear') was prearranged to signal that relations with Britain, the United States and Russia were 'in danger' and could trigger emergency actions by consuls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon hearing the code words, consuls were instructed to destroy sensitive documents (burn papers) and to follow prearranged contingency measures. The committee record notes controversy over whether intercepted broadcasts were genuine code signals or ordinary weather reports and whether such coded signals were actually received at monitoring stations.
